acceptanceCriteria: A maintained test or measurement at two store sizes shows that the work done under the writer lock in a lease commit does not grow with ticket count (CAL-V0-026).
Checkpoint recovery semantics are unchanged: a crash after the lease commit still recovers the same canonical state.
body: Found 2026-10-06 while fixing V1-0845 (branch claude/rc2-darwin-guard-locked-scan, commit e0fa13eb, base b7b21205, Darwin 25.6.0, go1.27.1). After V1-0845 moved the darwin change-guard Sweep outside the writer lock, `commitLease` in internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go still calls `retainCheckpoint` while it holds the writer lock (journal/checkpoint.go:64 encodes, store/guards.go:119 writes). Retention traverses, sorts and encodes the whole canonical map, so locked lease work still grows with ticket count, contrary to CAL-V0-026. Expected: locked work independent of store size, for example by retaining the checkpoint after the lock is released or making retention incremental. Actual: O(store) work under the lock. Inferred from source, not yet measured; the V1-0845 spec and build log record it as the remaining store-size cost.

title: Tasks lease commit retains the checkpoint under the writer lock in O(store) time
